**Subject: Order TH-48217 not received — replacement or full refund required by 13 November**

Dear Tiny Hands Edu Supplies Customer Service,

I’m writing again about order TH-48217, placed on 21 October, which I have still not received despite the tracking showing it as delivered. After two emails and a phone call, I’m very frustrated that I still have neither the supplies I paid for nor a clear commitment to resolve this.

I paid R1,640 by card, including R95 for delivery, for six tubs of finger paint, four bags of playdough, 200 paper plates, googly eyes, glitter glue and two rolls of brown paper. These are supplies for my class at Bergview Pre-Primary in Plumstead, paid for out of my own pocket.

The tracking states that the order was delivered on Tuesday, 3 November at 11:42 and signed for by “M. Adams”. Nobody by that name works at our school. Our gate guard, Uncle Faizel, keeps a record of every delivery, and there is no entry for this parcel on 3 November. I have also checked the delivery address on my order, and it is correct.

I emailed on 4 November and again on 6 November. Both times, I received the same response: “We have escalated your query to our courier partner.” When I phoned on Friday, I spent 38 minutes on hold, only to be told that nothing could be done until the courier completed its investigation, which could take 10 working days.

I understand that you need to investigate what happened with your courier. What I do not accept is being left out of pocket, with no supplies and no meaningful assistance, while that happens. I placed my order with Tiny Hands Edu Supplies, paid your company and did not choose the courier. I expect you to take responsibility for resolving the missing delivery rather than directing me to sort it out with a third party.

These materials are not simply sitting on a wish list. My class made their mask patterns last week, and I have been telling the children that the paint is “coming soon” for a week. We need the supplies to make props for our end-of-year concert on 27 November. The delay is now affecting our preparation time.

As a teacher who spent R1,640 of my own salary on materials for my class, I cannot reasonably be expected to pay again or wait indefinitely. I have ordered from you three times before without any problems, which makes the handling of this situation particularly disappointing.

Please arrange one of the following **by Friday, 13 November**:

- A replacement order, delivered to the school at no additional cost; or
- A full refund of R1,640, including the R95 delivery charge, to my original payment method.

Please have someone respond personally, address the delivery discrepancy and confirm which solution you will provide and when. Another template saying the matter has been escalated will not resolve this.

If I do not receive a substantive response and a resolution by that date, I will pursue a chargeback through my bank and leave an honest review of my experience. I would much rather resolve this directly with you, but I need the supplies or my money back.

Kind regards,  
[Your name]  
Bergview Pre-Primary  
[Contact number]
